ledger.sentence: The World Health Organization (WHO) issued its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity on 7 October 2026.
The WHO describes them as evidence-informed recommendations for managing obesity in children and adolescents.
ledger.note: Search 22: 'how health systems and health workers can deliver evidence-based, people-centred care'. [second pass: edited to unsupported correction: Retrieved text says 'evidence-informed recommendations'; 'people-centred care' and 'guidance for health systems and health workers' not seen in retrie]

ledger.sentence: There are two documents: one for children aged 29 days to under 10 years and one for adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.

The recommendations cover diet, physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep, behaviour-change and digital health interventions, medicines, bariatric surgery, weight-management devices and combined approaches.
ledger.note: Search 1 list: dietary interventions, physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep, behaviour changing interventions, digital health interventions, pharmacotherapy, bariatric surgery and weight-management devices, multimodal interventions.

ledger.sentence: The WHO strongly recommends structured changes to diet, behaviour and physical activity for children and adolescents with obesity.

The WHO says medicines, surgery and devices are not the foundation of care for children and adolescents with obesity; comprehensive support for healthy eating, physical activity and behaviour change is.
